title: Parmesan Crusted Tilapia
description:
We first had a dish like this at Kelly’s, that local Boalsburg hangout with a giant bull mounted on the roof. Known as a steakhouse, Kelly’s also makes some pretty good seafood dishes too, especially Parmesan Crusted Halibut Cheeks, which this should be called, but it’s typically very hard to find Halibut Cheeks, even when it’s in season.
This recipe works best with thin, firm fillets, such as halibut, tilapia, red snapper, catfish, orange roughy, etc. The fish is coated with seasoned Parmesan cheese and quickly sautéed. The cheese forms a delicate crust which compliments the fish in both flavor and texture. If small fillets are not available, use larger ones and cut them into smaller pieces.
ingredients: ½ cup of flour for the Parmesan
directions: Start by preparing the Parmesan flour mix. Mix parmesan cheese with 1/2 cup of flour in a shallow bowl.
Dredge the Tilapia fillets in plain flour, shake off any surplus flour, and dip them in egg.
Use the Parmesan flour mix to coat the Tilapia fillets.
Heat up a non-stick frying pan and pour some of the olive oil into it.
Place the Parmesan crusted Tilapia fillets in the frying pan and fry them until they are brown on both sides, turning once, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Remove the browned fillets from the pan and keep them warm.

In the picture on this page, you see big caper berries. These are very tasty, but you can use the smaller ones as well (they often come in two smaller sizes – like BBs or a little larger, like little peas.
For this meal, we also served the fish with spaghetti, but not the usual spaghetti pasta; rather, it was spaghetti squash. This is really tasty, different, and very easy.

Just halve spaghetti squash lengthwise and scrape out the seeds. Then sprinkle a little salt and pepper and a coating of olive oil or spray and put cut sides down in a roasting pan. Cook at 350 degrees for about 45 minutes. Remove from the oven and when cooled slightly, scrape out the spaghetti with a fork. You could add a little butter or more salt and pepper to taste. And, it will improve more with some of the extra sauce from the fillets.
Add some more olive oil to the pan and sauté the garlic in the oil.
Add white wine, capers, and chicken stock to the frying pan. Squeeze lemon juice from the lemon over the frying pan and season with salt and pepper.
Allow the sauce to reduce by half.
Remove the sauce from the heat and add the butter.
Place the Parmesan crusted Tilapia fillets on warmed serving dishes and pour sauce over them.
